who had been governor of Erbil.
They used to hang him by his feet about a cubit above the ground,
and beat upon his feet until he fainted.
And immediately they would take him down and beat upon his chest and upon his back,
until he fell down as if dead.
And again they would place fire in a frying pan,
and hang it upon his chest.
And in this way they inflicted bitter tortures upon him,
until they took from him about fifty thousand dinars.
And when he could not endure the tortures,
at times he cast himself into the Tigris River,
hoping perhaps he would drown and find relief from the anger, tortures, and blows.
Mas'ud bar Qawti, however,
because he was sick,
they did not subject to blows.
They feared lest he should die,
and his wealth perish with him.
Indeed, they treated him with empty promises,
saying that if he gave them one hundred thousand pieces of gold,
he would remain in his honor,
and no one would harm him.
That Mas'ud, however,
since he was not being scourged by them,
thought that they were according him honor,
and became even more arrogant,
and used harsh words with them.
They, however, in their cunning,
partly with scourgings and blows,
and partly with threats and intimidations,
exacted that amount from him.
And they took him with them to Erbil,
and there they killed him on Monday of Passion Week,
four days into the month of Nisan of that same year.
And upon his son they put a wooden yoke and imprisoned him.
And his brother Shihab al-Din fled,
and they searched for him diligently,
but did not find him.
And on his account, a certain Dubays from the village of Beth Sahraye was killed,
because he had hidden in that village for some days,
and then departed and left.
And when they questioned Dubays about him,
he denied it and swore that he had not seen him.
And when they seized a young boy and beat him,
he confessed and showed them the place where he had been.
And when they were confirmed that he had been with them,
they took the wretched Dubays to Mosul,
and there they killed him,
and the common folk stoned his corpse.
And after his murder,
the people of Mosul also made an accusation against another young man,
alleging that he was an adulterer and committed fornication with Arab women.
And him also they killed,
and dragged his corpse through the streets of the city,
and piled wood upon him,
and burned him with fire.
